newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Pill scare cost Organon 70 mln dfl in 96.
newsitem.headline: Pill scare cost Organon 70 mln dfl in 96.

text.p: Last year's oral contraceptive pill scare cost Akzo prescription drugs unit Organon some 70 million guilders ($36.9 million) in lost operating revenues, Akzo Chairman Cornelis van Lede told a results news conference.

"We are very proud that the pharmaceuticals activities were able to increase operating revenues despite the 70 million guilders of operating profits lost as a result of the pill scare," Van Lede said.
Pharmaceuticals booked 1996 operating income of 795 million guilders, up from 750 million guilders in 1995.
Van Lede said that Organon's results were expected to pick up in 1997. "We think the pill problems have bottomed out, although there are still some after-effects," he said.
Germany recently said it would extend its restriction on the so-called third generation of low dosage oral contraceptive pills, linked in some studies with an increased risk of thrombosis.
Van Lede said Akzo was contesting the restrictions.
Organon's third-generation contraceptive pills include top-seller Marvelon.
Van Lede said some progress had been made in opening up the Japanese market for oral contraceptives.
A Japanese government report presented to a special Health Ministry committee this week declared the low-dose birth control pill safe and effective.
There was speculation that official approval from the Japanese authorities might be forthcoming by mid-way through next year, Van Lede said.
-- Lien van der Leij, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000
